title: Checkpoints 4a & 4b Walkthrough
subtitle: the retry fix + the model picks

beats.narration: Section four has two checkpoints: repair a broken retry loop, and pick the model for three scenarios. If you haven't done both, pause — everything past this card is answers.

elements.text: ⏸ do both checkpoints first — answers ahead

beats.narration: The retry loop has one defect wearing three faces. Sleeping for zero seconds means no backoff at all — every retry fires instantly, and against a rate limit each instant retry is another request that deepens the very limit you're waiting out. Meanwhile the bare except retries everything, including terminal statuses that will fail identically every time. The corrected version does three things: it honors retry-after from the response when present, it grows the wait exponentially with jitter and a cap when the header is absent, and it re-raises terminal statuses so a bad request fails fast.

elements.code:
except Exception:      # ✗ retries terminal errors too
    time.sleep(0)      # ✗ zero backoff — instant hammer

beats.narration: Now the model picks. Millions of short classifications, with the small model holding the bar on the eval: Haiku. The deciding constraint is cost at volume — paying more buys nothing the eval can see. The dependent refactor where a wrong early step is expensive, and the mid tier misses the hardest cases: Opus. Quality on hard reasoning when mistakes are costly. And the mixed traffic, mostly lookups with a little synthesis: route it — a cheap default with a big-model override, because a single model either overpays the simple requests or underperforms the complex ones. In every scenario, the tell is the deciding constraint: the one thing that would change if you swapped the model.
